# Thanksgiving Hymns Column 11 — The EMET Bible (Literal)
**Translator:** EMET | **Source:** 1QHa (Cave 1), Col. 11 | **Condition:** well preserved

---

**11:1** I thank You, O Lord, for You have dealt wondrously with dust, and with a vessel of clay You have acted mightily.

**11:2** And what is it? I was taken from dust, and pinched from clay. I was formed as a source of uncleanness and shameful nakedness,

**11:3** a heap of dust, kneaded with water, a dwelling of darkness, a structure of clay, that returns to dust

**11:4** at the appointed time, and the path of the vessel of dust. And what shall the clay reply, and the one formed by hand?

**11:5** What counsel shall it understand? You have dealt wondrously with dust, and with a creature of clay You have done mightily.

**11:6** And what shall one born of woman be reckoned before You? He was kneaded from dust, and his dwelling is the food of worms.

**11:7** He is pinched clay, and to dust his longing returns. What shall clay reply, and that which is formed by hand?

**11:8** What counsel can it understand?

**11:9** But You, You have placed in my mouth a song of thanksgiving, and upon my tongue a psalm of praise, and the circumcision of my lips in a domain of rejoicing,

**11:10** and I shall sing of Your covenant-faithfulness and Your might all the day; continually I shall bless Your name.

**11:11** I shall recount Your glory among the sons of men, and in the abundance of Your goodness my soul delights.

**11:12** And I know that Your mouth is truth, and in Your hand is righteousness, and in Your thought is all knowledge,

**11:13** and in Your strength is all power, and all glory is with You.

**11:14** In Your anger are all judgments of affliction, but in Your goodness is abundance of forgiveness,

**11:15** and Your mercies are upon all the sons of Your good pleasure.

**11:16** For You have made them know the counsel of Your truth, and into Your wonderful mysteries You have given them insight.

**11:17** For the sake of Your glory You have purified a mortal from transgression, that he may sanctify himself

**11:18** unto You from all impure abominations and the guilt of unfaithfulness, to be joined

**11:19** with the sons of Your truth and in the lot with Your holy ones, to raise up from the dust the worm of the dead

**11:20** to an eternal council, and from a perverse spirit to Your understanding,

**11:21** and that he may take his stand before You with the everlasting host and the spirits of knowledge,

**11:22** to be renewed with all that is and shall be, and with them that know in a common rejoicing.

**11:23** And what is flesh compared to this? What creature of clay can do wondrous things?

**11:24** He is in iniquity from the womb, and until old age in the guilt of unfaithfulness.

**11:25** And I know that righteousness does not belong to a mortal, nor to a son of man the way of perfection;

**11:26** to God Most High belong all works of righteousness, and the way of a mortal is not established

**11:27** except by the spirit that God has formed for him, to perfect a way for the sons of men,

**11:28** that all His works may know the strength of His might and the abundance of His mercies

**11:29** upon all the sons of His good pleasure.

**11:30** And as for me, trembling and quaking seized me, and all my bones were broken,

**11:31** and my heart melted like wax before a fire, and my knees became like water poured out on a slope,

**11:32** when I remembered my guilt and the unfaithfulness of my fathers, when the wicked rose up against Your covenant

**11:33** and the miscreants against Your word. And I said: Because of my transgression

**11:34** I have been abandoned far from Your covenant. But when I remembered the strength of Your hand together with the abundance of Your mercies,

**11:35** I strengthened myself, and I rose, and my spirit held fast its stand against the onslaught,

**11:36** for I leaned upon Your covenant-faithfulness and the abundance of Your mercies. For You atone for iniquity,

**11:37** and purify a mortal from guilt by Your righteousness.

---
*EMET notes: Column 11 is one of the best-preserved columns in 1QHa. The hymn reflects the dualism of human frailty (clay/dust) and divine grace characteristic of Qumran theology. "Vessel of clay" (yetzer ha-chomer) preserved literally. "Covenant-faithfulness" for hesed. "Sons of Your good pleasure" (bene retzonekha) -- standard Qumran self-designation.*
